item.text: I’ll stay inside this repo and keep this tight. First I’m going through Prism as requested by the local instructions so I can find the execution path for `-X` without wandering.
Prism MCP wasn’t exposed here, so I’m falling back to the local Prism CLI for repository discovery. I’m looking for the `-X`/exec batching implementation now.

The failure path is clear: batch mode currently collects every path, builds one `Command`, and lets the OS reject it. I’m checking available dependencies/platform support so the fix can split batches using the system argument limit cleanly.
Small tooling wrinkle: this Prism CLI has a slightly different `read` syntax than the MCP-style notes. I’m asking it for the exact form, then I’ll edit only the execution module.

item.text: The repo already has `libc` on Unix, which gives us `sysconf(_SC_ARG_MAX)` without adding dependencies. I’m going to split `-X` invocations by an argument-size budget, preserving the existing sorted order and fixed command args.
I’ve got the shape of the fix. The edit is small but a bit careful: add a byte-budget helper, rebuild one command per chunk, and merge the exit codes if several chunks are needed.
I spotted one ordering edge right after the patch: fixed args that appear after a placeholder need to stay after the path chunk. I’m tightening that before running the narrow test.
The batching logic now preserves command argument order. I’m running the focused `exec` tests to catch compile and behavior issues in this module.

item.text: The focused test still passes, with only a pre-existing lifetime warning in `src/filesystem.rs`. I’m taking one final status snapshot so the wrap-up is precise.

Implemented the `-X` batching fix in [src/exec/mod.rs](/Users/tapabratapal/Projects/provasign/research/harness/results/fd-neutral-c-run-2026-09-19/work/sharkdp__fd__pr866.r3.gpt55_prism/src/exec/mod.rs). Batch execution now estimates the platform argument limit, accounts for environment/fixed args on Unix, and splits matched paths across multiple command invocations instead of building one oversized command.

Verified with:

```sh
cargo test exec::
```

It passed. The only warning was an existing lifetime-style warning in `src/filesystem.rs`, unrelated to this change.
